opportunities.name: arXiv topic search → Semantic Scholar citation lookup → note
opportunities.description: For a research topic and year, run an arXiv advanced search filtered to that year, open the top paper, look it up on Semantic Scholar to get its first author and citation count, and save a note that reads '<topic> (<year>): <title> by <author>, <N> citations'.
steps: On arXiv, click Search, then Advanced search
Clear the 'Search term...' box and type the topic
Under Date, tick the checkbox, choose 'specific_year', and type the year in YYYY
Click Search and open the top result (the arXiv:ID link)
Copy the paper title
On Semantic Scholar, type the title into the 'Search text' box and press Enter
Open the matching paper and read the first author and citation count
In Notes, click 'New note', type '<topic> (<year>): <title> by <first author>, <citations> citations', and press Enter

instances.values: topic='retrieval augmented generation', year=2023 → RIGHT: Retrieval-augmented Generation for Mainstream Hashtag Recommendation (Run-Ze Fan, 11 citations)
topic='protein structure diffusion', year=2024 → Accelerating Inference in Molecular Diffusion Models... (Ian Dunn, 7 citations)
topic='graph neural networks traffic forecasting', year=2022 → Efficient Traffic State Forecasting... (Bin Lei, 1 citation); interrupted by 1800flowers/mail activity, resumed at 1384.4

opportunities.name: Court case lookup on CourtListener + related US Code statute on Cornell LII → note
opportunities.description: For a case name, search CourtListener for its citation and decision date, look up the related US Code section on Cornell LII to get its title, and save a note that reads '<case>: <citation>, decided <date>. See <USC section> (<section title>)'.
steps: On CourtListener, click Case Law, then Search Case Law
Type the case name into 'Keyword(s) search with operators' and press Enter
Open the matching opinion '<case> (<year>)' and read the reporter citation and decision date
On Cornell LII, type the US Code citation into the search box and press Enter (or follow the statute link)
Open the /uscode/text/<title>/<section> result and read the section heading
In Notes, click 'New note', type '<case>: <citation>, decided <date>. See <USC cite> (<section heading>)', and press Enter

instances.values: case='Carpenter v. United States' → 585 U.S. 296 (June 22, 2018); statute 18 U.S.C. 2703
case='Bostock v. Clayton County' → 590 U.S. 644 (June 15, 2020); statute 42 U.S.C. 2000e-2
case='Miranda v. Arizona' → 384 U.S. 436 (June 13, 1966); statute 18 U.S.C. 3501

opportunities.name: Event planning: Peerspace venue search (+ flowers search and email summary)
opportunities.description: For an event type and city, search Peerspace for venues. In later occurrences the person also searched 1800flowers for a flower type and drafted an email summarising venue, catering, and flowers for a guest count.
steps: On Peerspace, click 'Enter your activity', select all, and type the event type
Click 'Enter a city, zip, or address', select all, type the city, and pick the suggested option
Click Search and review the venue results
On 1800flowers, click the Search box, select all, type the flower type, press Enter, and open the top product
In Mail, set To to the recipient and Subject to '<event> on <date>: venue, food, flowers'
Write a Body that summarises the guest count, venue rate, catering minimum, and the flower product with its price

instances.values: event='Team offsite', city='Chicago, IL, USA' (Peerspace only; several retries after location-field typos)
event='Birthday party', city='San Francisco, CA, USA'; flowers='tulips'
event='Product launch', city='New York, NY, USA'; flowers='white orchids' → White Phalaenopsis Orchid ($59.99); email to priya@example.com for 60 guests on Jan 14 (draft discarded)
